title_fb: A stranger offered you a coin flip. Would you take it?
hook: What if a stranger offered you a coin flip?
open_loop: Seed at line 3: the stranger smirks and on-screen text asks 'WHY SMILE?'. Line 6 asks outright 'Why does the stranger want you to quit?'. Both are paid off only in line 7 (over many flips, you win more money; +$25 per flip and -$25 HIM on screen) and the line 8 payoff.
payoff: To your brain a one hundred dollar loss feels like two hundred, so you say no. But over many flips you win more money, which is why the stranger wants you to quit. Your brain says no. The math says flip.

facts_used.claim: In the coin toss (win $150 / lose $100), most people decline.
Most people reject the 50/50 win $150 / lose $100 flip even though it pays on average (corroborating).
Meta-analysis mean loss-aversion coefficient 1.955, so a $100 loss feels like about $195 to the brain ('about two hundred'; research says about 2x).
Losses are treated as about twice as large as an equivalent gain; the ratio varies by context, so the stamp says 'about'.
Over many flips, +$25 per flip on average for you and -$25 for the stranger (zero-sum). A single flip is still a 50/50.

math_check: Per flip: 0.5*150 - 0.5*100 = +$25 on average (stranger -$25, zero-sum). Felt loss = 1.955*100 = $195.50, about 2x -> 'two hundred' (95% range $182.00-$210.20, all above the $150 win). One flip is still 50/50, so the spoken line says 'over many flips, you win more money' (100 flips: net loss only ~1.76% of the time).
changes_from_previous: Line 1: 'offers' -> 'offered' (standard English); titles updated to match.

Line 4: now 'To your brain, losing one hundred feels like two hundred.' (10 words, was 11). 'Nearly' dropped; hedge moved to the stamp 'FEELS LIKE ABOUT -$200' (research: about 2x, mean 1.955). Snap-zoom removed and the flee is timed after the stamp so it reads.
Line 5: 'But you want that money. So you flip.' gives Benny a motive for turning back, and sets up the tails bonk and line 6.
Curiosity seed planted early: at line 3 the stranger smirks and a 'WHY SMILE?' bubble appears (visual only, no extra words). Line 6 still asks the question outright; both pay off only at line 7.

Line 7: now 'Because over many flips, you win more money.' It no longer says each flip pays $25, so it does not contradict the -$100 just shown. The screen shows a flip counter, '+$25 PER FLIP' and '-$25 HIM' with the GULP gag.
Length: 70 spoken words (9+7+5+10+8+8+8+8+7) = 30.4 s at 2.3 w/s, 9 lines, 9 scenes. No ph fields. Kept the A/B ending and the line 8 payoff.
